On the eve of Apple's special event, Bloomberg published a new report detailing the decade-long development journey of Apple's foldable iPhone.

The report notably mentions that former Apple CEO Tim Cook was involved in the project, and reveals the possible price of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman pointed out that Apple engineers began developing the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after Cook returned from a business trip to China, he was "unusually excited" about foldable phones. He reportedly pushed Apple's hardware team to accelerate development of the company's first foldable device.

Cook generally "does not get involved in the conception of new products," so his participation in the foldable iPhone development added weight to the project:

Regarding the pricing of the foldable iPhone (internally referred to by Apple as iPhone Ultra), the company's original target entry-level price was US$1,999. However, due to rising component costs recently, the target price has been raised to US$2,199.

According to one source, Apple has discussed pricing its foldable product as high as US$2,199 in recent months, noting that various options were recently considered, and memory shortage issues have significantly pushed up Apple's cost targets. Some versions with larger storage capacities could be priced close to US$3,000. By comparison, the standard iPhone currently starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra for the first time tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be on-site at the Steve Jobs Theater to bring you in-depth coverage of all the details.
